summary.tldr: Creates a new offence for entering animal buildings or bringing in animals or things in ways that could expose animals to disease or toxic substances.
what_it_does: Creates an offence under the Health of Animals Act for entering a building or other enclosed place where animals are kept, without lawful authority or excuse, if that could expose the animals to disease or a toxic substance.
Creates an offence for taking an animal or thing into such a place if that could reasonably be expected to expose the animals to disease or a toxic substance.
Sets penalties for individuals who break the new rule, up to a $25,000 fine or 3 months in jail on summary conviction, or up to a $100,000 fine or 1 year in jail on indictment.
Sets penalties for other persons who break the new rule, up to a $100,000 fine on summary conviction or up to a $500,000 fine on indictment.
summary.background: The bill amends the Health of Animals Act. It adds a new section that is carved out from the Act’s general offence rule.
